program: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) — formerly called "Food Support" or "Food Stamps" in Minnesota's own manual glossary
agency: Minnesota Department of Children, Youth, and Families (DCYF) — but the Combined Manual itself is still hosted on the LEGACY Department of Human Services (DHS) domain
agency_short: Minnesota Department of Children, Youth, and Families (DCYF)
admin_note: County-administered by 87 county agencies plus 11 Tribal Nations — a different structure from Wisconsin's multi-county-consortium model (each Minnesota county runs its own office; there is no consortium layer). A genuine agency-name migration is in progress: Minnesota moved food/family-program functions from DHS to a newly created Department of Children, Youth, and Families (DCYF), but the authoritative eligibility policy — the Combined Manual — is STILL hosted on the legacy dhs.state.mn.us domain and content-management system as of this pack's build date, and several individual manual sections carry issue-date stamps ranging from 2014 to 2025, confirming real, uneven staleness across the manual (see PROVENANCE.md).
system: MAXIS (the county eligibility system); applicants apply through MNbenefits.mn.gov

verification.method: Direct fetch and pdftotext extraction of the Combined Manual's own Table of Contents/section-body PDF (dhs.state.mn.us, a legacy Oracle WebCenter Content host — the exact 'rot risk' the framework doc flagged going in) — the PDF turned out to contain full section body text, not just a table of contents, and every section body used in this pack was read directly from that extraction, not from a secondary summary. Several individual dollar-figure and status sections could NOT be independently re-verified against a live current-FY source in this pass: the dhs.state.mn.us drug-felons/ABAWD-adjacent page hit an active bot-detection wall (Radware/perfdrive challenge) on direct fetch, and USDA's own FY26 SUA values PDF and ABAWD waiver page both returned access-denied/bot-block responses to this pass's fetch attempts. Those gaps are disclosed, not silently guessed past — see PROVENANCE.md.
verification.gates: Cross-check: every claim traced to a specific Combined Manual section body (with its own issue-date stamp, visible directly in the extracted text) rather than a secondary paraphrase. One major finding: a widely-repeated secondary-source claim that Minnesota bans SNAP recipients with 2 failed drug tests for life is FLATLY CONTRADICTED by the Combined Manual's own current text (0011.27.03, issue date 11/2024) — Minnesota ended its drug-felony disqualification for SNAP as of 8/1/2023, made post-conviction drug testing OPTIONAL for agencies, and explicitly states a positive test or refusal to test may NOT be used to deny or terminate benefits. This is disclosed in the criminal-justice-disqualifications supplement and PROVENANCE.md as a corrected secondary-source error, not merely a finding. A second live, unconfirmed freshness risk: Minnesota's most recently reported statewide ABAWD waiver has a stated expiration of June 30, 2026 (per two independent secondary sources, not independently confirmed via a primary DHS/USDA source in this pass due to access barriers) — a date already past as of this pack's build date. `packages/snap-rules` stays parked — no MN StatePolicy entry exists yet (a pre-existing authoring gap, not a finding from this pack).
